The function \(f\) is differentiable for all real numbers. The point \(\left(3, \frac{1}{4}\right)\) is on the graph of \(y=f(x)\), and the
slope at each point \((x, y)\) on the graph is given by \(\frac{d y}{d x}=y^{2}(6-2 x)\).
(a) Find \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\) and evaluate it at the point \(\left(3, \frac{1}{4}\right)\).
(b) Find \(y=f(x)\) by solving the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=y^{2}(6-2 x)\) with the initial condition \(f(3)=\frac{1}{4}\).
